title: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler PreBind plugins must be rebuilt for the 1.36 framework (PreBindPreFlight returns a result)

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory

quote: PreBind plugin implementations need to be updated to return `PreBindPreFlightResult` from the `PreBindPreFlight` method; returning nil retains the existing sequential behavior.
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with out-of-tree PreBind plugins are affected; rebuild against the 1.36 framework before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build

title: Service spec.externalIPs is deprecated
quote: Added warnings and deprecation for Service `.spec.externalIPs`.
remediation: Every write to a Service that sets `externalIPs` now returns a deprecation warning; plan to move those Services to a LoadBalancer, a NodePort, or an ingress/gateway, since the field is on a removal path.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.externalIPs // []) != []) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + (.spec.externalIPs | join(","))'  # each of these warns on every write from 1.36

title: DRA drivers need resourceclaims/driver and schedulers resourceclaims/binding RBAC (DRAResourceClaimGranularStatusAuthorization is beta and on)

detection.reason: which ClusterRole belongs to a DRA driver is not derivable from the inventory; pods that reference claims mark the clusters that care

quote: Schedulers and controllers must be granted `update`/`patch` on `resourceclaims/binding`. DRA drivers must be granted `associated-node:update` or `arbitrary-node:update` (or patch equivalents) on `resourceclaims/driver`, restricted by their specific `resourceNames`.
remediation: Before upgrading, extend each DRA driver's ClusterRole with the `resourceclaims/driver` subresource (verbs `associated-node:update` or `arbitrary-node:update`, ideally restricted by `resourceNames`) and each external scheduler's role with `update`/`patch` on `resourceclaims/binding`; drivers upgraded through their vendors' 1.36-ready charts already carry it. Without it, claim status updates are forbidden and pods stay Pending.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.rules[]? | (.resources // []) | index("resourceclaims/status")) | .metadata.name'  # roles that only have resourceclaims/status need resourceclaims/driver (drivers) or resourceclaims/binding (schedulers) from 1.36

title: kubelet refuses to start with a negative imageMinimumGCAge

detection.reason: imageMinimumGCAge is kubelet configuration, not a collected object

quote: Added validation to prevent negative duration values for `imageMinimumGCAge`.
remediation: A KubeletConfiguration with a negative `imageMinimumGCAge` (previously silently treated as 0) fails validation on a 1.36 kubelet; set it to 0 or a positive duration before upgrading the nodes.
verifyCommand: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/configz" | jq -c '.kubeletconfig | {imageMinimumGCAge}'; done  # a value starting with '-' fails a 1.36 kubelet

title: Infeasible in-place resizes are rejected at admission instead of being marked Infeasible in status

detection.reason: the change is in how a future resize request fails, not in a stored field

quote: the request fails in admission rather than being marked as Infeasible in the Pod status later.
remediation: Automation that submits a resize and then polls the `PodResizePending` condition for `Infeasible` now gets a synchronous validation error instead; handle the error path.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resizePolicy != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # resizable pods whose callers may rely on the old Infeasible status

title: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins using Handle.WorkloadManager must be rebuilt for the 1.36 framework (PodGroupInfo → PodGroupState)

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory

quote: Renamed `PodGroupInfo` to `PodGroupState`, which may break custom scheduler plugins that use `Handle.WorkloadManager`.
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with plugins on the gang-scheduling API are affected; rebuild against the 1.36 framework before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build
coversNotes: Renamed PodGroupInfo to PodGroupState, which can break custom scheduler plugins that use
